documents.body:
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Seen 01/27/2025

Yearly UC follow-up. No bleeding, one or two formed stools daily on mesalamine 800 mg TID. This year she had osteonecrosis of the jaw after an extraction, now off zoledronic acid, and is followed by ENT. Hip AVN followed by orthopedics.

Exam: abdomen benign.

Plan: continue mesalamine. Return in one year. Call for any rectal bleeding or change in bowel habit.

documents.body:
AWV, subsequent. Turned 70 in January.

Interval year: jaw osteonecrosis after extraction (Sept), zoledronic acid stopped, biopsy benign; R hip AVN managed without surgery; UC quiet; bone mets stable on scans on letrozole.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. No falls - cane outdoors and on uneven ground. Home safety reviewed again, grab bar in tub already. Cognition unchanged. Advance care planning: she has now named her sister as health care proxy (form scanned).

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Oral: small area of exposed bone posterior lower jaw, unchanged appearance, no pus.

Plan:
- MTX labs today.
- ENT 3/17. Oncology bone scan in May.
- Vaccines current.
- Continue meds.

Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Seen 03/17/2025

Follow-up of bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the posterior mandible. Biopsy in December showed necrotic bone without malignancy. Zoledronic acid remains stopped. She rinses with chlorhexidine twice a day. Pain is now mild and occasional.

Exam: the area of exposed bone is smaller than in December. No purulence, no swelling, no lymphadenopathy.

Plan: continue chlorhexidine and conservative care. Return in 6 months or sooner with any drainage or swelling.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - regional hospital
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Arrival 08/24/2025 13:10

Chief complaint: left lower abdominal pain for 2 days.

HPI: 70-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis, breast cancer metastatic to bone and a history of bisphosphonate-related jaw osteonecrosis, with 48 hours of dull left lower quadrant pain. Nausea and less appetite, no vomiting. Also urinary frequency and burning. Never had pain like this before.

PMH: ulcerative colitis, metastatic breast cancer (bone), osteonecrosis of jaw, osteoporosis, RA, right hip AVN, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Home meds per outside list: HCTZ, atorvastatin, amlodipine, methotrexate, folic acid, prednisone, mesalamine, letrozole, calcium/vitamin D, chlorhexidine rinse; zoledronic acid also listed. NKDA.
Social: former smoker, social alcohol, retired teacher.

Exam: T 38.2 C, BP 145/90, HR 92. Uncomfortable. LLQ tenderness without rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds normal. Rectal exam unremarkable. No CVA tenderness.

Labs: WBC 14,000, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250,000. UA: trace leukocytes, no bacteria.
CT A/P with contrast: sigmoid wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding; no abscess or free air.

ED course: IV fluids and analgesia. Tolerated oral fluids. Pain improved.

Diagnosis: acute sigmoid diverticulitis, uncomplicated.

Disposition: discharged home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily x 10 days. Clear liquids, advance diet as tolerated. Follow up with PCP in 2-3 days. Colonoscopy once recovered, about 6-8 weeks. Return for worsening pain, persistent fever or vomiting.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in ED Sunday for LLQ pain x2 days, fever 38.2, WBC 14; CT showed uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. On Augmentin day 4 of 10. Pain much better, eating soft foods, no fever since Monday. Urinary burning gone. One loose stool a day, no blood.
O: VS as charted, afebrile. Abd soft, mild LLQ tenderness, no rebound.
A/P:
1. Acute sigmoid diverticulitis, improving. Finish Augmentin. Advance diet. Recheck CBC with her MTX labs in 2 weeks.
2. Colonoscopy in 6-8 weeks - referral to her GI. Reasonable to look again given UC and family history.
3. Immunosuppressed (MTX/prednisone) - low threshold to call if fever returns.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Date: 01/08/2026
Indication: follow-up after first episode of sigmoid diverticulitis (08/2025); ulcerative colitis; family history of colon cancer.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: good.

Findings:
- Ascending colon: 2.5 cm ulcerated mass. Biopsied. Tattooed distally.
- Sigmoid diverticulosis, no inflammation.
- Rectum and remaining colon: mild chronic changes consistent with quiescent colitis.
- Cecum reached; appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified.

Impression: ascending colon mass, suspicious for malignancy. Pathology pending. Will call patient and primary care with results; CT staging and surgical referral if confirmed.

Gastroenterology

orders.order: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast

documents.title: Colon biopsy - adenocarcinoma
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
GI called me: ascending colon biopsy = invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. GI has already told pt this afternoon.

Called pt. She is shaken but practical - "one more thing to get through." Explained next steps: CEA, CT chest/abd/pelvis for staging, colorectal surgery consult. CEA and preop labs ordered for Wed; CT Thursday. Colorectal surgery referral placed, GI also sending theirs. Will see her after surgery consult or sooner if wanted.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CEA 2.6. CBC, CMP normal. Copied to colorectal surgery and oncology.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast for staging. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Known sclerotic lesion in the T7 vertebral body, unchanged; known right 6th and 8th rib lesions without change.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease from colon cancer. Known osseous breast cancer metastases unchanged.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Tattoo marking in the ascending colon with mild focal wall thickening at the known mass, no pericolic stranding. No enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Liver without focal lesions. Sigmoid diverticulosis without inflammation. Known sclerotic T10 lesion unchanged. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Known ascending colon cancer without evidence of nodal or distant metastatic disease. Sigmoid diverticulosis without diverticulitis.

documents.title: Colorectal surgery consultation
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
COLORECTAL SURGERY CONSULTATION
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Date of service 01/22/2026

Reason: ascending colon adenocarcinoma found on colonoscopy 1/8/2026, done after sigmoid diverticulitis in August.

History: ulcerative colitis since 12/2022, quiescent on mesalamine; bone-only metastatic breast cancer, stable on letrozole; RA on methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg; osteoporosis; right hip AVN; jaw osteonecrosis; hypertension; hyperlipidemia. NKDA. Father had colon cancer.

Staging: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 1/15 without nodal or distant spread of the colon cancer; known bone lesions from breast cancer unchanged. CEA 2.6.

Exam: abdomen soft, nontender, no masses, no prior incisions.

Plan: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy, scheduled 2/9/2026. Risks including bleeding, infection, leak and blood clots reviewed. Enhanced recovery pathway; extended clot prophylaxis after discharge.

Colorectal Surgery

medications.drug_text: 0.4 ML enoxaparin sodium 100 MG/ML Prefilled Syringe
medications.sig: Inject 40 mg under the skin once daily for 28 days

reports.text: Specimen: right colon and terminal ileum, laparoscopic right hemicolectomy. Tumor: ascending colon, at tattoo site. Histology: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Depth: invades into muscularis propria (pT2). Lymph nodes: 0 of 19 involved (pN0). Margins: proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Background colonic mucosa with mild chronic changes, no dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, moderately differentiated, pT2 pN0 (0/19), margins negative. AJCC stage I.

documents.title: Discharge summary - right hemicolectomy
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - regional hospital
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955
Admitted: 02/09/2026   Discharged: 02/14/2026 (postoperative day 5)
Service: Colorectal Surgery

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon.
Procedure: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy, 02/09/2026.

Hospital course: uncomplicated operation. Enhanced recovery pathway. Diet advanced from postoperative day 1; return of bowel function on day 3. Mobilizing independently with cane. Pain controlled with acetaminophen. Hemoglobin 11.8 on day of discharge.

Pathology (02/12): moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT2 pN0 (0/19 nodes), margins negative - stage I. No adjuvant chemotherapy indicated; surveillance per colorectal oncology.

Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (HCTZ, amlodipine, atorvastatin, methotrexate, folic acid, prednisone 5 mg, mesalamine, letrozole, calcium/vitamin D, chlorhexidine rinse, acetaminophen as needed). NEW: enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily to complete 28 days after surgery.

Follow-up: colorectal surgery clinic in 8 weeks; primary care within 2 weeks. Call for fever, wound redness, worsening abdominal pain, leg swelling or shortness of breath.

events.reason: Shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain

conditions.label: Pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. No free subdiaphragmatic air.
Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. Normal axis and intervals. No ST-segment elevation or depression.

CT angiography of the chest, pulmonary embolism protocol. Filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental and subsegmental pulmonary arteries. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries patent. RV/LV ratio less than 1. No pulmonary infarct. Lungs otherwise clear. No pleural effusion. Known sclerotic T7 vertebral lesion.
reports.conclusion: Acute right lower lobe segmental and subsegmental pulmonary emboli without right heart strain.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - regional hospital
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Arrival 02/19/2026 15:20

Chief complaint: sudden shortness of breath and pain with breathing.

HPI: 71-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer and diverticulitis last August, now 10 days after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for colon cancer (discharged on postoperative day 5), on prophylactic enoxaparin. Two hours ago developed sudden shortness of breath and sharp chest pain on deep breaths. No recent travel. No leg swelling or leg pain.

Home meds per outside list: HCTZ, amlodipine, atorvastatin, methotrexate, folic acid, prednisone 5 mg, mesalamine, letrozole, calcium/vitamin D, enoxaparin 40 mg daily; zoledronic acid also on the list. NKDA.
Social: former smoker, quit about 13 years ago; social alcohol.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear to auscultation. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen with healing laparoscopic incisions. Legs without edema, erythema or tenderness.

Data: ABG on room air pH 7.49, PaCO2 32, PaO2 72, HCO3 24. Chest X-ray unremarkable. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes. High-sensitivity troponin I 6 ng/L. CT pulmonary angiogram: acute right lower lobe segmental and subsegmental emboli, RV/LV ratio <1.

Assessment: acute pulmonary embolism, postoperative, in a patient with active cancer. Hemodynamically stable, no RV strain.

Plan: enoxaparin increased to treatment dosing in the ED; supplemental oxygen 2 L to keep saturation above 92%. Admit to medicine for observation and transition to oral anticoagulation.

medications.drug_text: 0.4 ML enoxaparin sodium 100 MG/ML Prefilled Syringe

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (10 mg) by mouth twice daily for 7 days, then 1 tablet (5 mg) twice daily

documents.title: Discharge summary - pulmonary embolism
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - regional hospital
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955
Admitted: 02/19/2026   Discharged: 02/21/2026
Service: Hospital Medicine

Principal diagnosis: acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe segmental and subsegmental, without right heart strain.

Course: admitted from the ED 10 days after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (stage I colon cancer), on prophylactic enoxaparin at the time. Treated with therapeutic enoxaparin overnight, then started on apixaban. Oxygen weaned to room air by day 2, ambulating the hall without desaturation. Colorectal surgery saw her - incisions healing, no concerns. Hemodynamically stable throughout.

Discharge medications:
- STOP enoxaparin.
- START apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily. Duration at least 6 months; continue while cancer remains active - to be reassessed by primary care/oncology.
- Continue home medications otherwise unchanged.

Follow-up: primary care within one week. Return for worsening breathlessness, chest pain, bleeding or black stools.

documents.title: Prior authorization - apixaban
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Part D plan requested PA for apixaban 5 mg (hospital discharge Rx). Submitted with dx acute PE 2/19/26 and discharge summary. Approved through 2/2027. Pharmacy notified; pt had a 7-day supply from the hospital and picks up the rest today.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up, pulmonary embolism and colectomy

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Two hospitalizations this month: lap R hemicolectomy 2/9-2/14 for stage I ascending colon adenocarcinoma (pT2N0, 0/19, margins neg, no chemo), then readmitted 2/19-2/21 with acute R lower lobe PE while on prophylactic enoxaparin. Now on apixaban 10 mg BID through 2/26, then 5 mg BID. Enoxaparin stopped.

Today: breathing much better, no chest pain. No bleeding, stools formed, no blood. Eating smaller meals, weight down about 2 kg since surgery. Walking in the house and to the mailbox. Incisions healing.

Med rec: apixaban added; enoxaparin removed. Others unchanged: HCTZ, amlodipine, atorvastatin, MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5, mesalamine 800 TID, letrozole 2.5 daily, Ca/D BID, chlorhexidine rinse, acetaminophen prn. Zoledronic acid remains off (was still on the hospital's list - asked them to correct).

Exam: VS as charted, SpO2 normal at rest. Comfortable. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abd soft, port sites clean and dry. Calves soft, nontender, no edema.

A/P:
1. Acute PE, provoked by surgery, with active cancer - apixaban 5 mg BID after loading; plan at least 6 months, then reassess with oncology. Bleeding precautions reviewed. PA approved.
2. Stage I colon cancer s/p R hemicolectomy - surgery f/u April; CEA in May.
3. Postop weight loss - small frequent meals, recheck weight next visit.
4. Other chronic problems stable.
Spent >30 min reviewing records and coordinating. RTC 4 weeks (AWV).

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Recovering well from February: no more chest pain, back to her usual walks with the cane. On apixaban without bleeding. Appetite back.

PHQ-2: 1 - "it's been a lot," sleeping fine, enjoying things. No falls. Function: independent again.
Health care proxy on file (sister).

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen soft with healed port sites. No edema.

Plan:
- MTX labs today.
- Colorectal surgery 4/13, CEA in May; oncology bone scan in May.
- Apixaban - continue; revisit duration at 6 months (August/September).
- Vaccines current.

documents.title: Colorectal surgery follow-up
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Visit 04/13/2026

Two months after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for stage I (pT2 pN0) ascending colon adenocarcinoma. Course complicated by a pulmonary embolism on postoperative day 10, now on apixaban. She is eating normally with one to two formed bowel movements daily. Incisions healed.

Plan: no adjuvant therapy for stage I disease. Surveillance: CEA every 3-6 months, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis yearly, colonoscopy in one year (January 2027) with GI, who will also continue colitis surveillance. Return in 6 months.

Colorectal Surgery

Kidney and liver tests are normal for your methotrexate, and cholesterol is still on target. I've sent copies to surgery, oncology and rheumatology.

documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Visit 05/18/2026

Bone-only metastatic breast cancer on letrozole 2.5 mg daily, stable on bone scan 5/13 with no new lesions. Since last visit she was found to have a separate stage I colon cancer, resected 2/9, with a postoperative pulmonary embolism now treated with apixaban. CEA 2.1 in May.

Zoledronic acid remains held for jaw osteonecrosis.

Plan: continue letrozole. Given active metastatic disease I would favor continuing apixaban beyond six months if bleeding risk stays low; will discuss with primary care. Bone scan in 6 months.
